notes: THE DEFECT, IN recal_95's OWN SENTENCE. That round wrote 'a flat ceiling is a floor for everyone who reaches it, and Gasol was reaching it on size' — and then graded the 88 tier while leaving the BOTTOM of its own grading flat at 75. Dirk Nowitzki '07 is what that left standing: 7'0", BLK% 1.7 (0.8 a game, the 72nd percentile of his season), DBPM +1.2, no All-Defensive vote, ceiling evidence 0.000. His raw deterrent composite is 0.7798 — 38% of it the height percentile — the flat floor caps it at 0.7551, and the card prints rimprot 75 EXACTLY. The big d_score branch then takes it at 0.40 beside perdef 67 at 0.40, drb 88 at 0.17 and discipline 90: 74.41 x 1.1305 = 84.12, DEF 84, #20 of 239 in 2007, one under Battier '07 and two under Okafor '07. perdef 67 was already the restrained part; the card was carried by rim protection it had not earned.

THE FIX IS recal_92's BAR, READ ONE STEP EARLIER. recal_92 defines block evidence once — nothing below the 80th percentile of the season's block rate, the whole band at the 86th — and recal_95's ceiling grades UPWARD from the bar. The floor asks the prior question (is there any rim evidence at all), so it reads the same function shifted down by exactly one band width: full 75 at the bar, nothing at p74, the same linear grade between. Below that it falls to RIM_BAND_FLOOR = 0.55, which is not a new number: it is the 0.55 the two-stage deterrent scale itself starts from (ID2 = 0.55 + 0.47 x Prot(ID)), the number the sub-gate cap of 0.54 hands off to. Dirk '07 lands on it: rimprot 55, DEF 75, inside the ruling's 74 +-3.

MONOTONE, SUBTRACTIVE, AND NOTHING RISES. The graded floor is <= NOVOTE_FLOOR everywhere and enters a cap that can only bind downward, so on the whole pool 2,261 rimprot bars move and ZERO rise; 1,883 d_ovrs move, three of them UP (Eddie Robinson '01 +2, Jerome Kersey '86 +1, Wes Iwundu '19 +3) and those three rise only because a lower rimprot moves them off compute_ovr's big mix onto the perimeter one — the d_bigness ramp, not this file. 1,432 OVRs move, largest 5. A voted big is untouched by construction (his ceiling evidence is his vote share, unchanged), and so is every card at or above recal_92's block bar.

THE FRONTIER AND THE STOPPING PIN. The obvious form — grading the floor on recal_92's band UNSHIFTED — was measured first on the whole pool: it also lands Dirk '07 at DEF 75, but it costs Kevin Durant '19 (def 79 +-3 -> 68) and '24 (80 +-3 -> 75), and no choice of the floor's base rescues them, because Durant '19 sits at blk p81 with DBPM +0.1 and is ON the same flat floor Dirk is. Shifting the band is exactly what separates them: Durant '19 and '24 sit AT and ABOVE recal_92's bar and do not move a point, Dirk '07 sits a full band under it. The softer alternative — grading over [RIM_GATE, BLK_BAR], i.e. p60 to p80 — was measured too and does not reach: Dirk lands rimprot 66, DEF 80.

WHO ACTUALLY MOVES: no-vote bigs whose season block rate is under the 80th percentile — the class the flat floor was paying for height. Nikola Jokic '20 (0.6 bpg) DEF 78 -> 69, Kevin Durant '22 78 -> 68, Jack Sikma '89 83 -> 74, Bill Laimbeer '85 75 -> 67, Cooper Flagg '26 75 -> 66, Tiago Splitter '13 80 -> 71, Chris Bosh '10 71 -> 64, LaMarcus Aldridge '15 80 -> 72. WHO DOES NOT: every voted big (McHale '88 91, Malone '97 DEF 89, Garnett, Duncan, Mutombo, Wallace), every card at or above the block bar (Gasol '04 78, Kurt Thomas '09 79, Rich Kelley '81 79, Durant '19 and '24 78), every perimeter card (perdef, perimdisrupt and drb are byte-identical for all 10,000), and the whole top 12 of the attribute, name for name.

THE COMPARABLES THE FINDING NAMES NOW READ IN ORDER. Dirk '07 DEF 75 sits with Barkley '93 (75, rimprot 50, no votes, good DBPM) and Bird '87 (77, rimprot 60) — offensive stars with no defensive votes, which is the band the ruling puts him in — and he now reads ten under Battier '07 (85) and eleven under Okafor '07 (86) instead of one and two. His DEF rank in 2007 moves from #20 of 239 to #36.

TAXES: both crash-glass rows broke on the ORACLE edge (crash off +0.4478 at main's 0.55, crash def +0.4889 at main's 0.72) because their benefit reads a REBOUNDING attribute this round did not touch — what moved is the ovr>=55 pool the benefit is averaged over. Swept once from main's constants and re-ratified at the true midpoints, crashOff 0.55 -> 0.14 and crashDef 0.72 -> 0.59. All nine rows pass; the seven others held their bands untouched, hunt included.
cost: KEN NORMAN '94 (def 55 +-3, recal_136) IS NOW EXACTLY ON HIS BAND EDGE: 53 -> 52, error -3 of a tolerance of 3. He moves one point, and only through season smoothing off a neighbouring year. Any later round that lowers a no-vote big by one more point anywhere near him breaks that anchor.

THE CLIFF IS SHARP AND IT IS recal_92's OWN SHARPNESS: 20 card points across 6 percentile points of block rate (p74 to p80). That is the same width recal_92 already swings the voted ceiling over, but it now applies to a much larger class — every no-vote big in the pool. A later ruling that wants the band widened has to move BLK_BAR / BLK_FULL, which moves the voted ceiling too.

NOTHING IN THE VOTE CHANNELS WAS TOUCHED, deliberately: recal_135's reinforcement line ID = ID + 0.25 x (drep x hp) is another round's subject, and the whole of this change lives in the no-vote path where drep is 0 and that term pays nothing. The two rounds compose without conflict.

PIPELINE_VERSION is left at main's 157 per the integration rule, and this file records 157 for the same reason (the check is >=, so the integrator's stamp for the batch keeps it green). src/data/campaigns.json and src/data/opponents.json are regenerated in this commit (npm run opponents); the integrator re-derives them and re-sweeps the two taxes ONCE from main's constants for the merged batch, which supersedes 0.14 / 0.59 rather than stacking with them.
